issues: The rendered marks are a lollipop/dot plot with population-sized symbols, not the required cartesian_bar chart. This is a material chart-type fidelity failure even though the life-expectancy mapping is sensible.

The approximately 182-row static canvas is extremely tall and cannot function as a conventional publication figure at normal page size; reducing it to fit a page would make country labels and contextual values illegible.
The large title and legends consume substantial vertical space before the data, while the main plot requires extensive scrolling. The resulting information hierarchy is inefficient.

Population is encoded both through marker area and a numeric table column. The area encoding adds visual clutter and causes very populous countries to dominate nearby marks without materially improving the requested life-expectancy comparison.
The population-size legend uses the awkward label "1e+02K" instead of a publication-ready form such as "100K".

Region depends on color alone. Although the colors are fairly distinct, the orange and green categories may be harder to separate under some color-vision deficiencies, and there is no redundant region encoding.
Income level is encoded by shape, but small markers make circles, squares, triangles, and diamonds difficult to distinguish reliably across the dense display.

The chart does not print life-expectancy values in the contextual columns, so precise lookup requires estimating from the axis despite exact values being supplied for the other two quantitative fields.

The image visually appears to retain country-level records and uses country names, but the static rendering itself provides no explicit verification that exactly 182 records are present or that no record was duplicated.

The long horizontal stems resemble bars but do not encode magnitude as bar length from a meaningful baseline; they function as guides to point positions. This ambiguity further weakens compliance with the requested bar capability.
improvements: If cartesian_bar is mandatory, use actual horizontal bars with country_name on the categorical axis and life_expectancy_years on the quantitative axis, sorted consistently by life expectancy.

Because 182 categorical bars are unsuitable for one normal-sized static page, provide a vertically scrollable bar view or a paginated/multipage export while keeping every country recoverable. A synchronized searchable table would substantially improve entity lookup.
Keep population and income per person as formatted table or tooltip fields rather than additionally sizing the primary marks by population.
Add an exact life-expectancy value column, formatted consistently to one or two decimal places, to support precise comparison.
Use a compact title and legend block so that the data begins closer to the top of the canvas.
Replace scientific-style legend text with human-readable labels such as "100 thousand", "11 million", and "1.5 billion".
Use a color-vision-tested region palette and provide a redundant cue or explicit region column where feasible.
State the validated record count in a small metadata note, for example "182 countries; all observations: 2025; no missing values".
For a publication export, split the complete ranked list into clearly numbered pages or provide a compact companion table rather than shrinking the current 182-row figure.
